deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes axiomatize a 'topologie modérée' (tame topology) over a field R, essentially a real closed field such as ℝ, with a subfield R_0 of 'constants'. There is a class 𝓜 of 'modérées' (tame) subsets of the R^n, subject to axioms M1, M2, …, M11. There are tame maps and tame functions, and 'espaces modérés' are tame subsets of R^I. This is close in spirit to a structure in the sense of o-minimality, with the extra datum R_0, which plays the role of parameters or definable constants.

Step 1: inverses of tame functions. The previous page states two corollaries. First, a tame function f on a tame space X is invertible in the ring of tame functions iff f has no zero on X. Second, the equivalent form: if A ⊂ R^* is tame, then the graph {(x, x^{-1}) : x ∈ A} is tame. This page gives the proof. The graph equals {(x,y) ∈ R^2 | xy = 1, x ∈ A}. Suppose some tame B ⊂ R^* contains {x^{-1} | x ∈ A}. Then the graph is the inverse image of the point 1 under the tame map A×B → A·B ⊂ R, (x,y) ↦ xy. The marginal note seems to say that {1} is tame (1 ∈ R_0, so {1} ∈ 𝓜). Inverse images of tame sets under tame maps are tame, so the graph is tame.

Step 2: Corollary. R_0 is a subfield of R. It is closed under ring operations because polynomial maps over R_0 are tame. It is closed under inversion by step 1 applied to a singleton.

Step 3: collapsing a tame subset (begun here, finished on p. 23). Let X be a tame space and Y ⊂ X a tame part. Suppose Y is an intersection of fibres of tame functions, Y = ∩_α f_α^{-1}(e_α) with e_α ∈ R (referring to axiom M6). Replacing f_α by f_α − e_α, one may suppose (OPS = 'on peut supposer') that Y is the common zero set of tame functions f_α. Let (g_β)_{β∈J} be tame real functions realizing an embedding X ⊂ R^J, e.g. coordinate functions. Consider the family {f_α} ∪ {f_α g_β}. All of these vanish on Y and define Y as their common zero set.

On p. 23 it is shown that this family separates the points of X∖Y. If x, y ∈ X∖Y are not separated by the f_α, pick α with λ = f_α(x) = f_α(y) ≠ 0 and β with g_β(x) ≠ g_β(y). Then f_α g_β(x) = λ g_β(x) ≠ λ g_β(y) = f_α g_β(y).

Hence, under the axioms M1 (and MF, M11), the following holds. If Y is the common zero set of a finite family of tame functions, there is such a family F : X → R^N with F(Y) = {0} that is injective on X∖Y. So F realizes the quotient X/Y (Y collapsed to a point) as a tame space. Purpose: building tame quotients and collapse constructions inside the axiomatic framework, toward the 'dévissage' and topological results the notes aim at.
errors: The inversion argument is conditional: it assumes a tame B ⊃ {x^{-1} | x ∈ A} exists. Whether that is guaranteed is not settled on this page. It presumably requires another axiom, e.g. tame images under tame maps, or that R^* is tame, in which case one may take B = R^*. As written, this is a gap unless B = R^* is allowed.

The collapsing construction needs the defining family of f_α to be finite, and needs the embedding X ⊂ R^J to use finitely many g_β, for X/Y to land in a finite-dimensional R^N. This is only made explicit in the proposition on p. 23. On this page the index sets I and J are arbitrary.

Minor: the family f_α, f_α g_β separates points of X∖Y and sends Y to a single point. It does not by itself prove that the induced bijection X/Y → image is a homeomorphism or that the image carries the quotient topology. Later this needs closedness or properness arguments; the p. 23 parenthetical '(lorsque X/Y est un espace modéré)' hints at this.

ideas.what: Graph of x ↦ 1/x on a tame subset of R^* is tame, via the preimage of 1 under multiplication; consequently tame non-vanishing functions are units in the ring of tame functions
ideas.modern_name: Definability of field inversion / units in rings of definable functions in o-minimal structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in o-minimal geometry (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s); immediate in any structure expanding a field
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only called for programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), without such details

ideas.what: The constant subfield R_0 (points of the tame structure over the base) is a field
ideas.modern_name: dcl(∅) is a subfield / field of definable constants

ideas.what: Collapsing a tame zero set Y ⊂ X to a point via the functions f_α and f_α·g_β (zero on Y, separating points off Y)
ideas.modern_name: Definable quotient X/Y / collapse of a closed definable subset; analogous to the standard real-algebraic collapsing trick
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in real algebraic geometry (e.g. Bochnak–Coste–Roy) and o-minimal topology (van den Dries, Tame Topology and o-minimal structures, 1998, on definable quotients)

missed.claim: Historical record: Grothendieck worked out a concrete axiomatic system (axioms M1–M11, MF, with a base field R_0 of constants) for tame topology, including routine closure lemmas and a quotient/collapse construction. This apparently predates or parallels the o-minimal axiomatics of van den Dries (1984) and Pillay–Steinhorn. The mathematics on this page is routine; its interest lies only in documenting the shape of his axiom system.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Helps historians compare Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' with o-minimality, e.g. his use of a constant subfield R_0 and of collapse constructions. No new theorem for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is elementary closure properties of a tame structure plus a standard point-separation trick for collapsing a zero set. It is only of historical interest as part of Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatization of tame topology.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'En effet, c'est aussi l'ens. des' rather than 'l'image de'; the set {(x,y) | xy = 1, x ∈ A} is the graph itself.
'si on suppose qu'il existe [crossed out] B ⊂ R^*?, B ∈ 𝓜, contenant l'ens. {x^{-1} | x ∈ A}, on gagne' rather than 'contenant l'image … on procède'.
'car l'ens. est la partie modérée de A×B image inverse de 1 ∈ A.B' rather than 'l'image est …'. The vertical marginal note under '1 ∈ A.B' likely asserts that {1} is tame ({1} ⊂ 𝓜 / ∈ 𝓜).
'Cor' is written over a crossed-out word; read 'Cor R_0 est un sous-corps de R'.
'𝓜_b' is probably 'M6' (a reference to axiom M6): '… qui soit intersection [de fibres] des (M6) comme'.
'des fonctions modérées réelles réalisant un plongement X ⊂ R^J' rather than 'et une plongement [?]'.
Last line: 'Considérons les f_α, les f_α g_β — elles sont toutes nulles sur Y, et'; the second family is f_α g_β, not g_β (confirmed by p. 23).
